page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of shared L3 cache. It features 16 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. A dedicated 402 GB local NVMe solid-state drive is bundled directly with the hardware profile. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations highlight competent single-threaded performance alongside limitations inherent to its lower core count. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1714.0 and a single-core stress-ng rating of 1617.89, placing it in the middle tier of single-threaded capabilities. Single-threaded gzip compression yields 26.36 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 6.5 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 3812.0 and PassMark CPU score of 6112.89, fall into lower percentiles due to the 4 vCPU allocation. Memory throughput tests show 29.2 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22.26 GB/sec for large-block writes.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, the c3-standard-4-lssd couples general-purpose compute with fast local NVMe storage, eliminating the need to over-provision vCPUs merely to obtain local SSD capabilities. However, network configuration tradeoffs include zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The configuration is well matched for mid-tier web serving, intermediate staging databases, local caching nodes, CI/CD runners, and lightweight data transformation workloads that benefit from direct NVMe scratch space.

The processor supports advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX.
